text: Genesis 6 sets a world corrupt to its foundations beside one man who walked with God (6:9). The narrator gives the corruption without softening. Every imagination of the human heart is only evil continually (6:5), the earth is filled with violence (6:11), and Yahweh is sorry that he made man (6:6). Noah receives no commission to reform any of this. His task is to build. More words go to the ark's specifications (6:14–16) than to the corruption that makes the ark necessary, and the reason is that Noah builds to a measure he did not set. The ark exists as dimensions before it exists as wood. Of Noah's part the narrator records one thing only: he did all that God commanded him (6:22). Noah is called righteous before he lifts a tool (6:9). In this chapter his righteousness becomes visible as obedience, the willingness to build what God, who has looked upon the whole earth (6:12), says will be needed.
